summary: V2 test deferral inherits the v1 Decision 9 rationale (no XCTest target) but adds a substantially larger and more security-critical surface area: iframe sandbox boundary, postMessage allowlist, frameInfo defense-in-depth, atomic disk cache CRUD, ZIP staging/HTML rewriting, blob URL lifecycle, parallel section streaming, and CSP correctness. Several of these (postMessage payload validation, scope_hint/topicIndex bounds checking, atomic file rename, manifest concurrency, ZIP path-traversal) are exactly the class of defects that hand-trace audit + manual QA tend to miss because the failure modes are stateful, race-prone, or only manifest under adversarial input. Deferral is defensible ONLY if (a) follow-up scope explicitly lists every v2-specific path, (b) Pre-deploy QA includes adversarial test cases beyond happy-path Instruments scenarios, and (c) at least the security boundary tests (sandbox + postMessage + scope validation) are upgraded from 'follow-up' to 'pre-merge' for v2. Current spec satisfies (a) at high level but is vague on individual cases; (b) is partially addressed via 5 Instruments scenarios; (c) is NOT addressed — the spec keeps everything in follow-up. The follow-up entry in tasks/todo.md still references v1 modules only and has not been updated for v2 paths. The Pre-deploy QA Instruments check covers ARC retain-cycle paths (cache, exporter, iframe lifecycle) adequately for happy/error scenarios but does NOT cover atomic-write torn-state recovery, manifest-corruption recovery, or concurrent navigation-during-write races. Overall verdict: needs_improvement — deferral is defensible but follow-up scope and pre-merge gates need explicit v2 expansion before merge.

findings.issue: tasks/todo.md still enumerates ONLY v1 test modules (InsightSSEParserTests, InsightMarkerParserTests, InsightSessionTests, GraphRAGFolderMapReduceTests, InsightScopeHintValidationTests, InsightCancellationRaceTests, InsightResourceCapTests). Two of these are dead in v2: InsightMarkerParserTests (marker parser is removed) and the v1-specific shape of InsightSSEParserTests. Tech-spec Decision 9 v2 says the follow-up 'expands to cover v2 paths' and lists 7 new critical paths, but the actual file at tasks/todo.md has NOT been updated. Acceptance Criteria line 504 ('V1 follow-up TODO in tasks/todo.md updated with v2-specific paths') is stated but the work to update is implicit — not assigned to any wave/task explicitly. If merge happens before todo.md is updated, the v2 critical paths will silently fall off the follow-up scope.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit task (e.g. inside Wave 5 Task 8 or as a dedicated Task 8.5) that updates tasks/todo.md to: (1) remove InsightMarkerParserTests entirely (marker is deleted), (2) rename InsightSSEParserTests to AIProviderClientStreamingTests with v2-relevant scope (still covers Phase 2 streamCompletion), (3) add 9 new test modules: AIProviderClientToolCallTests (skeleton schema validation + fallback path), InsightSkeletonParserTests (defensive parser for malformed tool_use input), PostMessageAllowlistTests (5-type filtering, payload schema validation, topicIndex bounds), FrameInfoDefenseTests (rejection of non-main-frame messages — requires WebKit test harness or stub), InsightCacheAtomicCRUDTests (write/read/manifest atomic rename, torn-write recovery, concurrent reader-during-write), InsightArchiveExporterTests (staging dir construction, HTML rewriting correctness, asset copy, ZIP exit-code handling), BlobURLLifecycleTests (creation per session start, revocation on session close, no leak across sessions), Phase2ParallelismCapTests (exactly 5 concurrent, gated scheduling, cancellation propagates to in-flight section tasks), and IframeSrcdocCSPTests (CSP meta string correctness, sandbox attribute exact value, no allow-same-origin, lib blob URLs only). Pin owner and date inline. Make this update a hard prerequisite for closing Task 8 (block merge until todo.md diff is committed).

findings.issue: The v1 deferral was justified by test-audit because v1's critical paths were either (a) hand-trace verifiable with committed fixtures (SSE parser, marker parser) or (b) manually reproducible in pre-deploy QA. V2 introduces critical paths that fail BOTH criteria: (1) InsightCache atomic write — a partial-write/crash-during-rename scenario cannot be reliably reproduced manually (would require killing the process at the exact filesystem-syscall boundary); (2) Phase 2 parallelism cap — verifying 'exactly 5 concurrent, no more' under live API calls is non-deterministic; (3) postMessage payload schema validation — adversarial payloads (oversized, type-confused, prototype pollution) require systematic fuzz coverage that hand-trace cannot match; (4) topicIndex bounds checking — off-by-one in either direction is silently wrong, not crash-visible; (5) ZIP staging dir HTML rewriting — incorrect rewriting (relative path, lib ref) only manifests when the exported ZIP is opened in Safari, which IS in the manual QA but a single happy-path file is not adversarial coverage. The v1 test-audit PASS rationale ('committed fixtures + dual audit hand-traces + four-scenario Instruments') does NOT carry over to these v2 surfaces because there are no equivalent fixtures and the failure modes are not happy-path-visible.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) commit equivalent fixture coverage for v2: (i) Tests/Fixtures/insight-skeleton-sample.json (already planned in Task 1), (ii) Tests/Fixtures/insight-skeleton-malformed/*.json (5+ malformed cases — missing required field, wrong type, oversized array, recursive nesting, invalid enum value — each documented with expected fallback behavior), (iii) Tests/Fixtures/postmessage-payloads/*.json (5+ adversarial payloads — extra fields, missing required, type confusion, oversized string, out-of-range topicIndex), (iv) Tests/Fixtures/insight-cache-stale/ (a pre-built stale session dir to verify cleanup logic ignores it); OR (b) raise these test paths from follow-up to pre-merge and bite the bullet on XCTest target setup as part of v2 (would add an estimated 1-2 days but would give v2 the regression gate it needs given its larger surface).

findings.issue: The 5 Instruments scenarios cover ARC retain-cycle paths well (a happy + 2-3 expand + close, b error + retry + close, c rate-limit + close, d export ZIP + close, e breadcrumb-back + close — solid coverage of session/cache/exporter/iframe lifecycle). However, several v2-specific failure modes are NOT exercised by these scenarios and are NOT testable from outside the running app: (1) atomic write recovery — what happens if app crashes mid-rename? Spec says 'next session uses fresh sessionUUID; stale dir from prior session ignored' but there is no scenario that verifies stale dirs do NOT cause cleanup of fresh session data, do NOT block disk space indefinitely, do NOT contaminate manifest. (2) navigateTo race — what if user clicks breadcrumb while Phase 2 is still streaming, then quickly clicks forward? Section delta forwarding is keyed by lastForwardedSectionLength[sectionId] per node — if the active node changes mid-delta, deltas could be applied to wrong node's iframe. (3) deepDive payload race — same M1 race from v1 audit, now with sectionId+topicIndex but still racey if user double-clicks during navigation. Decision 9 v2 says M1 is 'more specific — verify race resolved or document as still present' but no scenario explicitly tests this. (4) Iframe srcdoc reset during section streaming — what if navigateTo fires while N parallel section tasks are mid-flight? Tasks should be cancelled, but cancellation is cooperative; in-flight onDelta callbacks may still try to forward to a now-different iframe. (5) Blob URL revocation race — if session closes while iframe is mid-load referencing blob: URLs, does the iframe error gracefully or hang? (6) ZIP export with deep tree (50+ nodes) — staging dir builder iteration is silent on failure if a single node read fails; verify partial-failure semantics.
findings.recommendation: Expand T12 Instruments/manual scenarios with 4 adversarial cases: (f) Crash-recovery: kill MarkView process (Activity Monitor → Force Quit) during Phase 2 streaming; restart, open insight on same folder, verify (i) new sessionUUID created, (ii) old session dir under .insight-cache/ remains but is NOT read or cleaned, (iii) no manifest contamination. Document expected stale-dir disk usage. (g) Navigate-during-stream race: open insight, wait for Phase 1, during Phase 2 click breadcrumb to root (back to skeleton-only state), then immediately click a deep-dive — verify the previously in-flight section task does NOT post deltas to the new iframe and does NOT corrupt cache. (h) Rapid double-click on deep-dive button: verify M1-equivalent race documented; either resolved or explicit user-visible behavior (e.g. second click is queued or dropped). (i) Large-tree export: programmatically generate a 30+ node session, click Export, verify ZIP completes within reasonable time, all nodes present, breadcrumb nav in Safari works. Each scenario must have explicit pass/fail criteria, not just 'check it works'. Consider also a 6th scenario for blob URL lifecycle: verify in Web Inspector that blob URLs created at session start are revoked at session close (URL.revokeObjectURL called) — leak here would accumulate ~1-4MB per session in browser-process memory.

findings.location: tech-spec.md Decision 9 + Risks table 'Tests deferred — same risks as v1'
findings.issue: The risk-table entry 'Tests deferred — same risks as v1 (silent SSE bugs, etc.)' understates the v2-specific risk delta. V2 has DIFFERENT risks than v1, not the same: (1) v1 had a markdown rendering pipeline where bugs are visually obvious (text appears garbled); v2 has an iframe sandbox boundary where bugs are silently security-critical (postMessage allowlist gap = arbitrary parent-frame action). (2) v1 had no disk cache; v2 has atomic-write semantics that, if broken, leave undetectable corruption (manifest references nonexistent nodes, or vice versa). (3) v1 had no ZIP export; v2 has shell-out to /usr/bin/zip with user-controlled destination URL where path-traversal in node IDs could write outside staging dir. (4) v1 had no parallel scheduling; v2 has 5-concurrent withThrowingTaskGroup where cap-violation under load could trigger Anthropic 429 cascades. The phrase 'same risks as v1' invites reviewers to apply v1's PASS verdict by analogy without examining the new failure surface. This is the precise anti-pattern the v1 test-audit warned against in its 'gap' section: 'no automated regression gate — future PRs can re-introduce regressions and won't fail any automated check until next manual QA cycle'. V2 makes that gap larger.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the Risks table entry to be specific: 'Tests deferred — v2 introduces NEW risk classes vs v1: (a) iframe sandbox boundary correctness (postMessage allowlist + payload schema + frameInfo defense) — silent security failure if regressed; (b) atomic disk write semantics (rename, manifest CRUD) — silent data corruption if regressed; (c) ZIP staging path safety — potential write-outside-staging if node IDs are not sanitized; (d) parallel scheduling cap — potential rate-limit cascade if regressed. Mitigation: (1) frameInfo guard provides defense-in-depth for (a); (2) cleanup-on-close + fresh-UUID-per-session bounds (b) blast radius; (3) UUID-based node IDs prevent (c); (4) gated scheduling pattern from GraphRAG round-1 fix battle-tested for (d). Compensation: pre-merge security audit (T10) hand-trace + 5 Instruments scenarios + 4 adversarial scenarios (see expanded T12). Follow-up XCTest infrastructure adds regression gate within 2 weeks of merge.' Also add explicit decision: do these v2 risks justify upgrading 1-2 specific test modules (PostMessageAllowlistTests, InsightCacheAtomicCRUDTests) to pre-merge instead of follow-up? Make the upgrade-vs-defer decision an explicit user-facing question, not an implicit defer.

findings.location: tech-spec.md 'Acceptance Criteria' — Iframe sandbox security (Decisions 2 + 3) checklist
findings.issue: Acceptance criteria for sandbox + frameInfo + postMessage allowlist + topicIndex bounds are stated as binary checks (e.g. 'iframe srcdoc starts with <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> exactly') but are verified only by static grep (per Agent Verification Plan table). Static grep verifies the string is PRESENT in source; it does NOT verify the runtime behavior is CORRECT. Specifically: (1) grep confirms `frameInfo.isMainFrame` token appears in WebViewBridge.swift but does NOT confirm the guard rejects iframe-originated calls (would require a WebKit-level test or live adversarial poisoned-md smoke); (2) grep confirms 5 postMessage types appear in index.html but does NOT confirm the parent rejects a 6th type (would require live test posting an unknown type and verifying it is dropped); (3) grep confirms topicIndex appears in handler but does NOT confirm bounds-checking logic is correct (off-by-one would pass grep). Manual QA prescribes 'poison a .md file → run insight → check no spurious bridge calls reach Swift' as the smoke for frameInfo, but that is a single happy-adversarial case; it does not enumerate the 4-5 attack vectors a fuzz test would cover (eval-style payload, prototype pollution, unicode normalization tricks, URL constructor in postMessage payload, recursive-nested object).
findings.recommendation: For each of the 4 binary acceptance criteria with security implications (sandbox attr, frameInfo guard, postMessage allowlist, topicIndex bounds), add a specific manual smoke test in T12 that exercises the negative case: (1) Sandbox: in Web Inspector, evaluate `document.querySelector('iframe').sandbox.toString()` — assert exact value 'allow-scripts'. Then attempt `iframe.contentWindow.parent.document.body.innerHTML = 'pwned'` — assert SecurityError or no effect. (2) frameInfo: temporarily inject test JS into iframe srcdoc that calls `window.webkit?.messageHandlers?.bridge?.postMessage({type: 'insightRequestSave'})`. Verify in Swift logs that NO handler invocation occurs (either webkit.messageHandlers undefined per sandbox semantics, OR the frameInfo guard rejects). (3) postMessage allowlist: in parent Web Inspector, run `window.postMessage({type: 'insightRequestNavigate', payload: {url: 'https://evil.com'}}, '*')` — assert parent rejects (no Swift call). (4) topicIndex bounds: post `insightDeepDiveClicked` with topicIndex=-1, topicIndex=999, topicIndex=null, topicIndex='5' (string), topicIndex={}; assert each is rejected. Document each test's expected log/UI signature. These take ~15 minutes to run but provide the runtime verification grep cannot.

findings.location: tech-spec.md Risks table — 'KaTeX webfonts in iframe blob context'
findings.issue: Risk states 'Validate during T5; if blob URL doesn't carry fonts, base64-inline the .woff2 files'. This is a known unknown deferred to implementation. If validation discovers fonts don't work, the fallback (base64 inline) bloats every iframe srcdoc by the woff2 size (~50-100KB per font × multiple fonts = 200-400KB per node × 50 nodes = 10-20MB cache bloat per session). No test or acceptance criterion covers 'KaTeX renders correctly in iframe with math content'. This will be discovered in manual QA only if the user happens to open insight on a folder with math content.
findings.recommendation: Add to T12 manual QA: 'Open insight on a folder containing at least one .md file with KaTeX math (e.g. `$E = mc^2$` or block math). Verify math renders correctly in iframe. If fonts missing or rendering broken, T5 fallback (base64 inline) was incorrectly resolved.' Also add to acceptance criteria: 'KaTeX math content (inline `$...$` and block `$$...$$`) renders correctly in iframe with no missing-font warnings in iframe console.'

findings.issue: Task 11 (Test Audit) description is essentially identical to v1 Task 11 ('Meta-audit: tests deferred per Decision 9. Verify tasks/todo.md follow-up scope expanded with v2-specific paths'). Risk: the v2 Task 11 will produce a PASS verdict by template-matching v1 (same 5 checks structure) without independently re-evaluating whether v2's larger surface justifies the deferral. The v1 test-audit's PASS rationale was specific to v1's compensation set (SSE/marker fixtures, hand-trace coverage of every parser branch, 4 retain-cycle scenarios). V2 Task 11 must NOT inherit that rationale; it must re-derive whether v2's compensation is adequate.
findings.recommendation: Strengthen Task 11 description to require v2-specific evaluation: 'V2-specific test audit (NOT a copy of v1 Task 11). Verify: (1) tasks/todo.md follow-up scope updated with v2 paths AND v1-only paths removed (marker parser tests); (2) Pre-deploy QA includes adversarial scenarios beyond the 5 happy-path Instruments (per recommendations from this test audit); (3) NEW v2 fixtures committed: insight-skeleton-sample.json + at minimum 3 malformed variants for fallback verification; (4) for each of the 4 v2 security boundaries (sandbox, frameInfo, postMessage, topicIndex), grep-only verification is supplemented with at least one runtime smoke test in T12; (5) explicit decision documented (yes/no) on whether PostMessageAllowlistTests + InsightCacheAtomicCRUDTests should be upgraded from follow-up to pre-merge given v2 surface — if no, justify; (6) carry-over from v1 audit: M1 race resolution status (sectionId+topicIndex makes it more specific but not necessarily resolved). Write report logs/audit/test-audit.md with explicit FAIL gates if any of the 6 are unmet.'

findings.issue: ZIP export uses /usr/bin/zip via Process. Acceptance criterion verifies 'exits 0; atomic move'. Not covered: (1) /usr/bin/zip exit codes other than 0 (zip can return 12 for nothing-to-do, 18 for could-not-open-source, etc.) — does the Swift wrapper handle each, or does any non-zero trigger the same error path? (2) Concurrent export — if user clicks 'Save Archive' twice rapidly, does the second invocation use a fresh tmp staging dir or collide? (3) Destination URL with sandbox-permission edge cases (writing outside the user-selected URL's parent — should be impossible since user picks via NSSavePanel, but verify). (4) ZIP of empty session (root only, no children) — should produce valid 1-file archive. (5) ZIP of session where one node read fails — partial archive vs hard fail.
findings.recommendation: Add to T12 manual QA matrix: (a) export immediately after root generation (1-node session, no expansions) — verify ZIP opens and shows root only. (b) Click 'Save Archive' twice within 1 second — verify second click is either disabled, queued, or starts independently with separate tmp dir; verify no file collision. (c) Manually corrupt one cached node HTML (rm + create empty), then export — verify either hard fail with clear error or partial archive with warning, NOT silent success with broken node. Add acceptance criterion: 'ZIP export handles non-zero exit code from /usr/bin/zip with user-visible error containing exit code and stderr (sanitized).'

findings.location: tech-spec.md Decision 5 (Pre-bundled libs blob URLs) + Verification Plan
findings.issue: Verification Plan checks Chart.js SHA-256 against MANIFEST.txt (good). Not verified: (1) other vendored libs (Mermaid, KaTeX, Prism) SHA-256 also recorded in MANIFEST and verified at build time — Task 2 description only adds Chart.js; existing libs may or may not have SHA entries. (2) Build-time integrity check — what stops a tampered Chart.js from being committed if MANIFEST is updated to match? Current setup is honor-system (developer recomputes SHA). (3) Runtime integrity — the loaded blob URL content is not re-verified against MANIFEST; if app bundle is tampered post-install, no detection. The sandbox + CSP defense-in-depth limits blast radius, but a compromised lib with eval could escape via postMessage to parent.
findings.recommendation: Add to Task 2: 'MANIFEST.txt MUST contain SHA-256 entries for ALL vendored libs (Chart.js + Mermaid + KaTeX + Prism + any others), not just Chart.js. Add a CI/pre-commit check (or build-phase script) that recomputes shasum -a 256 for each vendored file and fails the build if MANIFEST entry doesn't match. This converts honor-system into automated gate.' Add to acceptance criteria: 'shasum -a 256 of every file in Resources/Editor/vendor/js/ and vendor/css/ matches its MANIFEST.txt entry; build script enforces.'
